record.paper_title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
record.original_question: Human and other contact networks are often not closed, isolated populations, but are connected across multiple population scales. When temporal contact networks at different scales all change over time, what epidemic and network dynamics emerge from coupling those scales together?

evidence.quote: In nearly all cases, static and temporal contact network models are composed of closed and isolated populations, but in our globally connected world human contact networks commonly have have far-reaching connections.
This may be addressed using a combination of contact network models at different population scales. What dynamics emerge when network changes occur over time at these different scales?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction in the literature on epidemic thresholds for temporal networks. While there is active work on multi-layer and multi-scale temporal networks (e.g., metapopulation models, multiplex temporal networks), no general theory characterizing epidemic thresholds and emergent dynamics for fully coupled multi-scale temporal contact networks appears to be established. The problem is therefore considered open.

status_evidence.title: Toward epidemic thresholds on temporal networks: a review and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews open questions on epidemic thresholds for temporal networks, including the need for multi-scale models coupling contact networks at different population scales.
status_evidence.claim: Multi-scale temporal contact network coupling is identified as an open research direction.
